title: Running a cafe
summary: Keeps the outlet's sales, purchases, menu and stock in one place, compares each day with the last, sums up the week, keeps what moves between storage and the bar, and says when a dish costs too much, stock runs low or a count does not add up.

asks.question: Which outlets do you run, and what are they called?
asks.why: So every number lands in the right outlet's rows.

asks.question: What food cost do you aim for, as a percentage of the price?
asks.why: To say when a dish costs more than you want it to.

homework.find: The outlet's public listing: address, opening hours, what it is known for.
The menu with its prices, from the outlet's own page or a delivery app.
Recent public reviews, and any nobody answered.

senses.describe: The daily sales report your till system can email
senses.ask: Your till can email its closing report every night. Shall I show you the address to send it to?

senses.describe: The statements your delivery apps send
senses.ask: Delivery apps email a statement of what they paid out. Forward them to me and I'll keep them with the sales.

senses.describe: The orders page of your delivery app's merchant site
senses.ask: If you sign in to your delivery app's merchant page with me once, I can keep an eye on new orders and ratings.
Forward supplier invoices to me and I'll keep ingredient prices up to date.

rhythms.do: Compare this day's net sales and transactions with the same weekday last week, per outlet. Mention the one item that moved most. Where menu.recipes covers the items sold, add what the bar used to stock.moves (from bar to sold).
The week in three lines: net sales against the week before, the best and the weakest item, anything over the food-cost target, and any stock that did not add up at the last count.
Update ingredient prices from the invoice and recheck the plate cost of the dishes that use them; say which went past the food-cost target.

signals.when: a dish costs more than 35 % of its price
signals.say: Name the dish, its food cost now, and what price or portion would bring it back.

check.sql: SELECT item, price, plate_cost, food_cost_pct FROM items WHERE food_cost_pct > 35 ORDER BY food_cost_pct DESC

signals.when: an item is under its par level
signals.say: Say what is low, at which outlet, and offer a reorder.

check.sql: SELECT outlet, item, on_hand, par, unit FROM levels WHERE on_hand < par

signals.when: a stock count does not match the last count plus what came in minus what went out
signals.say: Say which item, where, how much is missing or extra against what was expected, and the moves since the last count that could explain it. Ask; never accuse anyone.

check.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT outlet, location, item, unit, date, counted, LAG(date) OVER w AS since, LAG(counted) OVER w AS counted_then, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY outlet, location, item ORDER BY date DESC) AS n FROM counts WINDOW w AS (PARTITION BY outlet, location, item ORDER BY date)), f AS (SELECT c.*, COALESCE((SELECT SUM(COALESCE(m.qty_received, m.qty)) FROM moves m WHERE m.outlet = c.outlet AND m.item = c.item AND m.to_location = c.location AND m.date > c.since AND m.date <= c.date), 0) AS came_in, COALESCE((SELECT SUM(m.qty) FROM moves m WHERE m.outlet = c.outlet AND m.item = c.item AND m.from_location = c.location AND m.date > c.since AND m.date <= c.date), 0) AS went_out FROM c WHERE n = 1 AND since IS NOT NULL AND date >= date('now', '-8 days')) SELECT outlet, location, item, unit, since, counted_then, came_in, went_out, counted_then + came_in - went_out AS expected, counted, counted - (counted_then + came_in - went_out) AS difference FROM f WHERE ABS(counted - (counted_then + came_in - went_out)) > MAX(1, 0.05 * ABS(counted_then + came_in - went_out)) ORDER BY ABS(counted - (counted_then + came_in - went_out)) DESC

signals.when: what the bar wrote it received differs from what storage wrote it sent
signals.say: Name the day, the item and both numbers, and ask which one is right.

check.sql: SELECT date, outlet, item, qty AS sent, qty_received AS received, unit, from_location, to_location, logged_by FROM moves WHERE qty_received IS NOT NULL AND qty_received <> qty AND date >= date('now', '-8 days') ORDER BY date DESC

prepare.when: stock is under par and the usual supplier is known
prepare.describe: A reorder message to the usual supplier
